Costs and expenses are costs and expenses. If you have one supplier offering your raw material at $0.20/lb and another offering your raw material for $0.18/lb but further away, you can calculate how much money you would save in daily operating expenses by simply moving closer to the $0.18/lb manufacturer. When you apply this technique to all facets of a business (and trust me, they do), you get companies outsourcing jobs and shipping overseas to the cheapest labor they can find.

It's also not always a single factor that drives outsourcing: they might be able to skirt certain regulations and reduce the costs of certain raw materials by using techniques or materials that are illegal in their country of origin. Taxes (or government required expenses) might also be lower.

These decisions aren't made in a vacuum. They're scrutinized by accounting teams and proposed to management with a run down of the risks, cost, and expected payoff.
